Once upon a time, in a land called Dubai, I was living away from home for the first time.

Before Dubai, I applied to Qatar Airways. There was a long queue outside the hotel, and I was in it, wearing a blazer and a skirt, along with more than 900 other candidates. I made it to the final 14, and then I was cut. A few days later, Emirates had an opening. There were about 100 of us that time, and I got in.

Three months in Dubai, I was on the phone with my mom, crying, telling her I wanted to go home. I stayed for four years and five months. I asked “chicken or beef?” more times than I can count.1

After flying, I shaped a surfboard on the Gold Coast and tried carpentry back home.2

My head is often full of ideas.3

During the lockdown, I started Feelings Coffee, a box I wished existed. It was my first venture, right after my MBA. This time, the case study was live: real customers, me in every role, and the occasional curveball.4 After that, I went back to teaching Tagalog, this time on YouTube, as a one-woman show.5

I taught myself data storytelling before AI could do it for me,6 and I learned how to build websites.

When I don't know how to do something, I do my best to figure it out.

Today, I'm the Lead Storyteller at Good Cup.7

The three octopuses at the top of this page cover their eyes, ears and mouth.8 Tap one and it will take you where you need to go.

How I Can Help

AI can do a lot of the doing now. I believe what I bring is the way I see things, the way I listen, and the way I connect ideas and tell a story. Here's what that looks like if we work together.

Pedro · to help you see

How I see

I look at things from a different angle, and I connect ideas from places that don't usually meet: an airplane cabin, a coffee bar, a surfboard workshop, a spreadsheet.

I can help you:

  • Find a fresh angle for your brand, product or campaign
  • Come up with ideas when you're stuck
  • Turn your numbers into a story people understand
  • Ideation
  • Campaign concepts
  • Product experience
  • Data storytelling
Diego · to help you hear

How I listen

Flying taught me to read people from all over the world. Teaching Tagalog taught me to notice when someone is lost. Running a small business taught me that you can't read people's minds, so you have to listen.

I can help you:

  • Understand your customers and what they actually want
  • Talk to people across cultures
  • Figure out the real problem before jumping to a solution
  • Customer insight
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Research
Juan · to help you speak

How I speak

Storytelling is my day job. I write blogs, captions and campaigns, and I've been the one in front of the camera too.

I can help you:

  • Tell your brand's story in a way that sounds human
  • Write for your website, social media and emails
  • Build a simple website to put it all in one place
  • Storytelling
  • Copywriting
  • Content
  • WordPress and Framer

If any of this sounds like something you need, I'd love to hear about it. Send me an email.

If Life Had Chapters

Would we work well together? Here are a few chapters to help you decide.

  1. 1Chicken or Beef?More than four years as a flight attendant with Emirates Airlines.Emirates

    Planes were like a hop-on, hop-off bus.

    I rarely flew with the same person twice. My colleagues and passengers came from all over the world.

    It's impossible to fit my adventures in one paragraph. But if we had met on one of the flights, our conversation would have probably started with, “Chicken or beef?”

    • Cross-cultural communication
    • Service
    • Reading people
  2. 2SawdustAfter flying, I wanted to try things I had never done.Gold Coast

    I enrolled myself in a surfboard shaping workshop on the Gold Coast. Breathing in sawdust wasn't fun, but shaping the board was. There's something about tactile activities. Maybe it's the number of nerve endings on our palms… I haven't checked.

    Or maybe it's because I once wanted to be a furniture designer and a carpenter.

    • CarpentryJoined a carpentry workshop in Manila.
    • CookingLearned the way most people do: by trying, tasting and trying again.
    • 3D printingDesigning printable keychains. See chapter 8.
  3. 3I Have an IdeaThis one isn't tied to a point in time.Ideation

    “I have an idea” is something you’ll hear from me. Are they all good? No. But I’ll share them with you and test them.

    Some ideas stay small. Some turn into campaigns at work. A few turned into a coffee box, this website and three octopuses.

    • Ideation
    • Campaign concepts
    • Product ideas
  4. 4A Box of FeelingsA coffee box I wished existed.Feelings Coffee

    It started during the lockdown, an uncertain time for everyone. The original idea was closer to Leafly than to the sampler box it turned into.

    I was talking to one of my Tagalog students at the time, and through him I learned about startups. He was the first person who believed in the idea. He said it had bones.

    This was right after my MBA. In school, problems came as case studies: one subject at a time, already in the past. Feelings Coffee was happening live. I was dealing with real people and juggling marketing, operations, finance, logistics and sourcing all at once. Some things were within my control, and some weren't, like delayed deliveries and supplier problems.

    At first, it was all me. Then I learned to work with an illustrator: delegating, communicating, figuring out my strengths and weaknesses. It was an exercise in grit and perseverance.

    The boxes still live on Instagram.

    • Brand building
    • Copywriting
    • Visual direction
    • Customer experience
  5. 5NakakapagpabagabagTeaching Tagalog on YouTube.Tagalog

    After Feelings Coffee, I went back to Tagalog and focused on YouTube. I came up with the ideas and concepts, researched the topics, wrote the descriptions, stood in front of the camera, edited the videos, made the thumbnails and posted on Instagram.

    • Teaching
    • Video content
    • Clear explanation
  6. 6712 Flights, 92 Airports, 60 Cities, 35 CountriesI taught myself data storytelling and data visualization.Data storytelling

    One of the first stories I told with data was my own: how much did I travel as cabin crew?

    4.3years
    712flights
    92airports
    60cities
    35countries
    5continents

    AI can draw a chart in seconds now. But data only lands when people can understand it, so how you present it matters as much as the data itself.

    I made the dashboards below in Tableau, before AI could build them. I cleaned the data, looked for the patterns and decided what to show.

    I also learned how to build websites with WordPress and Framer. I built one for someone who became my mentor, and then I worked with her. She called me her “everything,” because I learned and did a bit of everything in my job. She once told me, “I don't expect you to know everything, but I expect you to figure things out.”

    • Data storytelling
    • Data visualization

  7. 7Lola Basyang Has a Day JobLead Storyteller at Good Cup.Present tense

    I'm in charge of the blogs and the captions for most posts. Ideation is part of everyone's job on the team, and I contribute ideas for social media and for campaigns.

  8. 8The Key of Ibong AdarnaIf you have the key, you can unlock many doors.Keychain studio

    Keychain Studio has a few keys. It also has three octopus keychains for 3D printing: see no evil, hear no evil and speak no evil, with octopuses instead of the three wise monkeys.

    I'm fascinated by octopuses. They have three hearts, blue blood and nine brains. They're so different, and that resonates with me. I've never really felt like I belonged anywhere, not even in my own family. That's not meant to sound dramatic. It's just the feeling of being different.

    It started with a visual idea: the octopuses turning gray. That reminded me of the Ibong Adarna, whose songs put you to sleep before it turns you to stone. There's a story behind the keychains, but I'm still in the process of writing it.

    I built a little studio to preview the colors and finishes before printing. I made it by experimenting with AI. Drag to spin them.

    see no evil · hear no evil · speak no evil

  9. 9Dear MomThis is a letter to my mom. I'm still working on it.A letter

    This section is my anchor. It keeps me grounded.

    I'd like to think my mom was the first person who loved me and the first person I loved, my first connection to this world, literally and figuratively. I know I've changed over the years, and I'll keep changing. But some things are worth keeping the same, and I don't want to lose sight of that.

    Dear Mom,

    When I was crying on the phone in Dubai, you were the one I called.

    The truth is, I don't know what to write to you yet. I just know it starts with thank you.

The end, for now
